events.title: Lincoln Signs the Thirteenth Amendment
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln signed the joint congressional resolution approving the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The amendment banned slavery and involuntary servitude, and it was then sent to the states for ratification.
events.significance: The amendment became the constitutional foundation for ending slavery in the United States, and it was ratified later in 1865.

events.title: The Oxford English Dictionary Begins Publication
events.description: The first installment of the Oxford English Dictionary appeared. It covered entries from A to Ant and started a project that would take decades to finish.
events.significance: It began what became the most authoritative historical record of the English language.

events.title: The Greensboro Sit-Ins Begin
events.description: Four Black college students sat down at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina, and refused to leave until they were served.
events.significance: Their protest inspired sit-ins across the American South and became a landmark of the civil rights movement.

events.title: Khomeini Returns to Iran
events.description: Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini flew back to Tehran after about 15 years in exile and was greeted by huge crowds.
events.significance: His return marked a turning point in the Iranian Revolution and led to the founding of the Islamic Republic.

events.title: Space Shuttle Columbia Disintegrates
events.description: Columbia broke apart while re-entering Earth's atmosphere at the end of its mission, and all seven astronauts on board were killed.
events.significance: The accident led NASA to investigate and reform its safety practices, and it contributed to the decision to retire the shuttle program.
